compiled_state.title: Wire cited_lines through CI defense pipeline + proximity-matching suppression filter
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Story A: F7b cycle-over-cycle convergence — wire existing cited_lines schema end-to-end through the CI defense pipeline so the suppression matcher can key on file+line proximity instead of description-prefix text.

## As-a / Goal
As a DSO maintainer, I want cycle ≥ 2 reviewer findings that re-cite the same code region as a prior defended finding to be auto-suppressed regardless of how the LLM rephrased the description, so that the CI llm-review job converges across cycles instead of generating fresh blocking findings on every push.

## Empirical motivation (PR #102 + PR #103 data)
- **PR #103 cycle 3**: 17 findings, ~70% within ±5 lines of a cycle-2 finding in the same file; three exact-line matches (runner.py:941 ×2, test-ci-defense-pipeline.sh:1 ×2, review-defense-store.sh:569). Forced admin merge override.
- **PR #102 cycle 2**: 19 findings, heavy proximity overlap with cycle 1's 28 findings — merge-to-main-pr.sh :416/:422/:1073 exact matches, sprint-story-review.yml :47 exact, test-merge-to-main-pr-resume-and-stale.sh :147/:153/:175 within ±9 of cycle 1's :138/:150/:152.

## Root cause
The schema already defines: cited_lines on findings (required, review-findings-schema.md:127), cited_lines_fingerprint on DefenseRecord (required, review-defenses.md), and a ±5-line proximity-overlap rule (review-findings-schema.md:203). **None of this is wired into runner.py.** _suppress_defended_findings (runner.py:369) keys on (severity, description[:80]) and ignores cited_lines entirely. The CI defense-record producer (mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh) also strips cited_lines, so even if the matcher were fixed it would have no anchor to match against.

## Scope
1. **Producer leg**: mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh (and any upstream emitter writing DEFENSE_RECORD lines) must include cited_lines for each defended finding. Today's records contain only severity, description, defense_text — confirmed by inspection of the PR #103 cycle-2 defense comment.
2. **Matcher leg**: _suppress_defended_findings in runner.py replaces description-prefix keying with file+line proximity matching against defended cited_lines using the existing ±5-line window. Same severity-downgrade outcome on match (to 'suggestion'), same telemetry.
3. Behavior preserved: defenses without cited_lines (legacy / pre-this-story records) fall back to the existing description-prefix matcher so older PRs continue working.

## Done definitions
- When this story is complete, mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh emits cited_lines on every DEFENSE_RECORD it posts.
- When this story is complete, _suppress_defended_findings in runner.py performs proximity matching using cited_lines (±5 lines per the schema rule).
- When this story is complete, a regression fixture replays PR #102 cycle 2 (28 cycle-1 findings as defenses → 19 cycle-2 findings as input) and asserts ≥ 60% of cycle-2 findings are downgraded.
- When this story is complete, a regression fixture replays PR #103 cycle 3 (33 cycle-2 findings as defenses → 17 cycle-3 findings as input) and asserts ≥ 60% of cycle-3 findings are downgraded.
- When this story is complete, defenses lacking cited_lines (legacy) still match via the existing description-prefix path — no regression on older PRs.
- When this story is complete, unit tests cover the proximity-matching function with overlap, no-overlap, exact-match, and legacy-fallback inputs.

## Out of scope
- relation/escape_rationale enforcement (deferred to Story B under same parent).
- cited_excerpt content-hash anchor (deferred to Story C, depends on 677d-a6a0).
- verifier-agent ruling integration (depends on 4100-95a4 decomposition).

## Dependencies and coordination
- RC-A (PR #103, merged) is a prerequisite — without DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE wiring there is no cycle ≥ 2 to suppress. ✓ in place.
- No dependency on 677d-a6a0; this story works with the cited_lines field that is already required.
- No dependency on 4100-95a4; this story ships standalone.

## Files touched (planning estimate)
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py — _suppress_defended_findings rewrite, ~80 LOC.
- plugins/dso/scripts/review-github-defense-store.sh and/or mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh — include cited_lines in DEFENSE_RECORD payload.
- tests/scripts/test-defense-matcher.sh (new) — proximity-match unit tests + replay fixtures.
- Possibly review-findings-schema.md if proximity-window constant needs to be made explicit.

## Acceptance fixtures
- tests/fixtures/pr-102-cycle-1-defenses.jsonl — 28 records derived from PR #102 cycle 1.
- tests/fixtures/pr-102-cycle-2-findings.jsonl — 19 findings from PR #102 cycle 2.
- tests/fixtures/pr-103-cycle-2-defenses.jsonl — 33 records from PR #103 cycle 2 defenses.
- tests/fixtures/pr-103-cycle-3-findings.jsonl — 17 findings from PR #103 cycle 3.

## Escalation Policy
Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue. Escalate when blocked.

comments.body:
## Design consideration to incorporate: regression-masking carve-out (RC-B gap analysis)

The proximity matcher as currently scoped suppresses any cycle ≥ 2 finding within ±5 lines of a prior defense. This has a subtle inverse-problem failure mode: when the autonomous-resolution loop's code change between cycles N and N+1 actually breaks the cited region (rather than fixing it), the new finding is a true regression caused by the resolver — and the matcher will silently downgrade it to 'suggestion' because it lands in proximity-window of the cycle-N defense.

The matcher has no signal today to distinguish 'LLM rephrased a defended finding' (suppress correctly) from 'the autonomous resolver introduced a regression in the defended region' (must NOT suppress).

**Acceptance criterion to add to this story**: the proximity matcher must check the diff between cycle-N HEAD and cycle-(N+1) HEAD; if the diff touches any line inside the cited_lines of a candidate defense (with the same ±5 proximity window), do NOT proximity-suppress findings matching that defense in cycle N+1. The schema already supports this — `DefenseRecord.story_branch_tip_sha` and `story_branch_base_sha` are present per review-defenses.md, and `load_for_region`'s SHA-range validation logic gives the orchestrator the SHAs needed to compute the inter-cycle diff. The matcher just needs to actually consult them.

**Recommended additional test case**: 'cycle 2 diff modifies a line cited by cycle-1 defense' fixture; assert no suppression and full re-review of the modified region.

**Related downstream concern (force-push interaction)**: PR rebase / force-push between cycles rewrites the cycle-N HEAD SHA. `load_for_region`'s SHA-range validation per review-defenses.md is the design answer, but the actual CI path computing `DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE` from prior persisted state doesn't visibly exercise the SHA-range path. Worth a fixture: 'cycle-2 starts → branch force-pushed → cycle-3 begins'; assert defenses from cycle 1 are correctly invalidated or preserved per the SHA-range rule. Could be folded into this story's acceptance or split off as a sibling test-coverage story.

Source: RC-B gap analysis, 2026-05-12. Filed alongside parallel comments on e7f3-2b45 (umbrella), 0b1b-8177 (Story B), jira-dig-1673 (defense citations).

## Preplanning Considerations (from Risk & Scope Scan)

- [Testing] Both stories modify runner.py — ensure unit tests cover legacy-fallback (no cited_lines) path AND new proximity path in the same test suite to avoid isolation gaps between Story A and Story B
- [Reliability] Regression-masking carve-out (from design note): if the autonomous resolver modifies a cited region between cycles N and N+1, the proximity matcher MUST NOT suppress the new finding. Implementation plan must add the diff-check acceptance criterion: check inter-cycle diff before applying proximity suppression. Test case: 'cycle 2 diff modifies a line cited by cycle-1 defense' — assert no suppression.
- [Testing] PR-103-cycle-2 and PR-102-cycle-2 fixtures require real finding data (severity, file, line numbers). Implementation plan must derive the exact suppression threshold (the ≥ 60% assertion) from fixture inspection before writing tests — this is SC1's explicit requirement.
